question: A 42-year-old woman, gravida 3, para 3 comes to the physician because of a 14-month history of prolonged and heavy menstrual bleeding. Menses occur at regular 28-day intervals and last 7 days with heavy flow. She also feels fatigued. She is sexually active with her husband and does not use contraception. Vital signs are within normal limits. Pelvic examination shows a firm, irregularly-shaped uterus consistent in size with a 16-week gestation. Her hemoglobin concentration is 9 g/dL, hematocrit is 30%, and mean corpuscular volume is 92 μm3. Pelvic ultrasound shows multiple intramural masses in an irregularly enlarged uterus. The ovaries appear normal bilaterally. The patient has completed childbearing and would like definitive treatment for her symptoms. Operative treatment is scheduled. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient has heavy menstrual bleeding" -> "Possible uterine pathology" -> "Pelvic ultrasound shows multiple intramural masses" -> "Diagnosis consistent with uterine fibroids" -> "Patient completed childbearing" -> "Definitive treatment desired" -> "Surgical intervention planned" -> "Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine device can reduce bleeding" -> "Considered as a pre-operative management option" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient has anemia with hemoglobin of 9 g/dL" -> "Heavy menstrual bleeding likely contributing to anemia" -> "Need to manage bleeding before surgery" -> "Tranexamic acid can reduce menstrual blood loss" -> "May be used as a temporary measure" -> "Not definitive treatment" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Patient has firm, irregularly-shaped uterus" -> "Indicates presence of fibroids" -> "Heavy menstrual bleeding is a common symptom" -> "Progestin-only contraceptive pills can help manage bleeding" -> "Not definitive treatment" -> "Less effective than other options" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Patient is sexually active and desires definitive treatment" -> "Leuprolide can shrink fibroids" -> "Used for pre-operative management" -> "Not a definitive treatment" -> "May delay surgery" -> 65%

CHAIN: "Patient has completed childbearing" -> "Desires definitive treatment for symptoms" -> "Estrogen-progestin contraceptive pills may not be appropriate" -> "Could exacerbate bleeding" -> "Not suitable for this case" -> 60%
analysis: The patient presents with heavy menstrual bleeding and anemia, likely due to uterine fibroids, as indicated by the pelvic ultrasound showing multiple intramural masses. Given that she has completed childbearing and desires definitive treatment, the most appropriate next step in management would be to provide symptomatic relief while preparing for surgical intervention. The Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine device (IUD) is effective in managing heavy menstrual bleeding associated with fibroids and can help improve her hemoglobin levels before surgery. Other options like progestin-only contraceptive pills and estrogen-progestin contraceptive pills are less effective for heavy bleeding due to fibroids compared to the IUD. Leuprolide is typically used for preoperative management but is not the first-line option for immediate symptom control. Tranexamic acid is a supportive treatment but does not address the underlying cause. Therefore, the Levonorgestrel-releasing IUD is the best-supported option for this scenario.
